analysis.title: How can I position for equity upside? (UBS House View Briefcase)
key_insights: UBS CIO says tech stocks are under pressure as markets adjust to elevated bond yields, firmer energy prices and persistent geopolitical risks, while earnings and economic activity remain resilient.

UBS advises staying invested through diversified exposure to cyclical and structural growth, and using market strength to reduce concentrated single-stock positions. Higher rates and energy costs call for selectivity, not a broadly defensive stance.
UBS treats AI as a structural investment opportunity. Risks are rising in the more capital-intensive parts of the buildout, where funding pressures and execution risks could reinforce each other.
UBS cites accelerating cloud growth and rising GPU rental prices as evidence that broader AI demand remains robust.
UBS forecasts aggregate AI capex of USD 1tr in 2026, USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028.
Market performance is concentrated, so a narrowly concentrated equity portfolio increases exposure to company-specific setbacks. UBS recommends diversification.

UBS expects a robust US economy, solid labor market, strong credit creation and continued fiscal support to support earnings outside the AI complex. Earnings growth outside the US also broadens the opportunity set.
Preferred US sectors are consumer discretionary, financials, health care, industrials and utilities.
UBS is positive on Eurozone equities and favors banks, consumer discretionary, health care, industrials, IT and Germany.
In Asia, equity valuations are at multi-decade lows and AI investment trends remain intact, supporting the earnings outlook. Japanese equities should also benefit.

Google Cloud revenue grew 103% y/y, up from 82% the prior quarter and 34% in the March quarter. Azure grew 48% for the three months to September versus 43% for the June quarter. Oracle's growth accelerated to 62% from 47%. Amazon's cloud unit accelerated for the sixth straight quarter.
UBS expects Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth of 25-30%, supported by AI investment, an improving industrial cycle and healthy aggregate consumption.
Investors with concentrated megacap tech positions can consider using rallies to rebalance into structured strategies that offer a degree of capital preservation.
UBS forecasts 15% earnings growth in Europe in both 2026 and 2027, supported by a manufacturing recovery, structural investment and operating leverage.

Investment view: positive returns expected across the US and most global markets. UBS suggests maintaining diversified core equity exposure, reducing concentrated single-stock positions, and considering capital preservation strategies where drawdown tolerance is limited.
